title: Niger Anticipatory Action: Drought
text:
This document describes the design of an anticipatory action trigger for drought in Niger, based on IRI seasonal forecast probabilities and an August rainfall observation.
The trigger has two independent arms — either can fire to release early action:

Forecast arm: fires when any two consecutive monthly IRI forecasts (January–June) are both among the top 5 most elevated “below-normal” years in the historical record.
Observation arm: fires when early August rainfall is among the bottom 5 driest years.

The trigger is calibrated against 28 years of data (1998–2025), targeting approximately a 1-in-3.5 year combined return period.

The IRI forecast probabilities are expressed as fractions (0–1) of the climatological below-normal tercile. The August observation is a standardised anomaly — lower (more negative) values indicate drier conditions.
The beta regression trend models are fit on the full 1991–2025 record to maximise sample size for estimating the long-term climate shift. The trigger threshold design uses 1998–2025 only, matching the period of reliable operational data.

title: Niger Anticipatory Action: Drought
text:
Detrending
IRI seasonal forecast probabilities for below-normal precipitation show a declining trend over 1991–2025. This likely reflects the partial recovery of Sahelian rainfall since the 1970s–80s drought era, alongside improvements in the IRI model’s baseline climatology. Without detrending, a historical percentile threshold would systematically favour recent years and underweight older drought signals.
We apply a two-step detrending procedure:

Beta regression — fits a trend curve bounded to (0, 1), appropriate for probability data. Divides out the trend so the series fluctuates around a constant mean.
Variance standardisation — fits a linear model to the absolute residuals over time, then rescales so the spread is constant across years.

The beta trend is fit on the full historical record (1991–2025); the variance model is also fit on all years. Both are then applied to the 1998–2025 analysis window.

Figure 1: Detrending pipeline for each forecast month. Blue = full-record beta trend; grey = raw observations. Col 1: mean-detrended series. Col 2: absolute residuals with linear spread fit. Col 3: fully detrended series.

text:
Forecast Skill

JAS SPI timeseries








Figure 2: JAS SPI (July–August–September Standardised Precipitation Index), 1998–2024. Negative (red) bars indicate below-normal seasonal rainfall.







Correlation with IRI forecasts
The plot below compares how strongly each monthly IRI forecast correlates with the JAS SPI outcome, before and after detrending. Negative correlations (plotted here as positive for readability) indicate that a higher “below-normal” forecast probability is associated with a drier season — a useful predictive signal.








Figure 3: Negative correlation between monthly IRI forecast and JAS SPI. Higher bars = stronger drought forecast skill. Detrending generally preserves or slightly improves skill.







ROC AUC — lower-tercile drought years
The ROC AUC summarises how well each monthly forecast discriminates between drought years (JAS SPI below the lower tercile) and non-drought years. An AUC of 0.5 is no better than chance; 1.0 is perfect.








Figure 4: ROC AUC for each monthly IRI forecast against the binary outcome (JAS SPI below lower tercile). Values above 0.5 indicate useful forecast skill.

text:
Trigger Design

Parameters
The trigger was designed over 28 years (1998–2025) using the full historical record detrending model. The selected thresholds fire in approximately 10 out of 28 years — a 1-in-2.9 combined return period.



Parameter
Value




Analysis period
1998–2025 (28 years)


Detrending model
Full historical record (1991–2025)


Forecast arm: trigger years
Top 5 of 28 ≈ 17.9%


Observation arm: trigger years
Bottom 5 of 28 ≈ 17.9%


Total trigger years
10 / 28


Combined return period
~1-in-2.9 years



The forecast arm fires when any two consecutive monthly forecasts (e.g. Jan+Feb, Feb+Mar, …, May+Jun) are both in the top 5 years. Requiring consecutive months adds persistence, reducing false alarms from single-month spikes.
The observation arm provides a safety net: it fires independently when the August rainfall observation is among the bottom 5 years, even if the forecast arm did not fire.

title: Niger Anticipatory Action: Drought
text:
Back-Transformed Thresholds
The thresholds above are defined in detrended space — a stationary series where the declining trend has been removed. To apply the trigger in practice, we need the equivalent threshold in raw forecast probability space for each future year.
The back-transformation inverts both detrending steps using the fitted models, accounting for the expected beta trend and spread at each year. Because the underlying trend in below-normal probabilities is declining, the raw threshold for 2026–2027 is lower than it would have been in the 1990s — the trigger will fire at a lower absolute forecast probability, reflecting the changed climatology.








Figure 5: Raw IRI forecast probabilities (grey) with beta trend (blue) and back-transformed trigger threshold (gold dashed). Red dots mark years that triggered in detrended space. Gold diamonds show the 2026 and 2027 threshold values.
